# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 55 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 55

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever does not hate his father and his mother cannot become my disciple.

**2** And whoever does not hate his brothers and his sisters and bear his cross in my way will not be worthy of me."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Hate"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "put me above." The Coptic moste = hate; the strong verb is present in both Thomas and Luke 14:26. Matthew softens to "love more than me" (10:37). Thomas preserves the Luke/Q form.

**"Bear his cross in my way"** — consensus. The phrase "in my way" is unique to Thomas and adds a qualitative dimension to cross-bearing: it is not any cross but the specific path of Jesus.

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- Luke 14:26-27: "If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple"
- Matt 10:37-38: "Whoever loves father or mother more than me... whoever does not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of me"
- Thomas is closest to Luke; the "in my way" addition is unique

---
